uk-cpi-2026-10.standing: The Office for National Statistics' monthly measure of how fast UK consumer prices are rising. The Bank of England targets 2% on it, and the September figure is the one used to uprate many benefits the following April.
uk-cpi-2026-10.recent: Economists have warned of 5% UK inflation if a US diesel ban goes ahead, which puts fuel at the centre of this release. The September figure shows where prices stood before any such shock, and it is the base a fuel-driven rise would build on.

fomc-2026-10.standing: The Federal Open Market Committee, the Federal Reserve's rate-setting body, meets eight times a year to set the target range for overnight lending between banks. Its decision moves the cost of borrowing in dollars worldwide.
fomc-2026-10.recent: Most officials have said they expect another hike by year-end, but the committee is split, and the September jobs count came in at 29,000 against 90,000 expected. Warsh has put price stability first after 5.5 years of inflation above target; this meeting settles whether a stalled labour market changes that order.

ecb-2026-10.standing: The euro area's central bank, whose Governing Council meets eight times a year to set interest rates for every country sharing the euro. Its decisions move the currency and the cost of government debt from Germany to Italy.
ecb-2026-10.recent: Inflation jumped to 3.8% in September, after a hike officials judged proportionate and not yet restrictive. The meeting weighs how much further to go against the heaviest debts, France first, where Moulin says no rescue is needed yet. Nominations to replace Isabel Schnabel, its leading voice for tighter policy, close the day before.

boj-2026-10.standing: The Bank of Japan's Policy Board, which meets eight times a year to set Japan's short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen, the yield on Japan's vast government debt and the cheap yen loans that fund investments abroad.
boj-2026-10.recent: Three sources said the bank is weighing a declaration that underlying inflation has reached its 2% goal, the test it has long set for leaving cheap money behind. Japanese yields jumped as a global bond sell-off deepened. This meeting is where the board says whether the goal is met, and what follows from saying so.

boe-2026-11.standing: The Bank of England's nine-member Monetary Policy Committee, which meets eight times a year to set Bank Rate. Its vote moves what British households pay on mortgages and what the government pays to borrow, and sterling moves with it.
boe-2026-11.recent: The committee decides ahead of the December hikes that markets are betting on at both the Federal Reserve and the ECB, after euro-zone inflation hit a three-year high and most Fed officials said they expect another increase by year-end. Its vote settles whether the Bank of England moves before that turn or waits for it.

fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Open Market Committee, the Federal Reserve's rate-setting body, meets eight times a year to set the target for overnight lending between US banks. Its decisions set the price of dollar borrowing worldwide.
fomc-2026-12.recent: Most Federal Reserve officials expect another hike by year-end, and this is the last meeting before it. The committee is split: inflation has topped its target for 5.5 years, yet September produced 29,000 jobs against 90,000 expected. Warsh has put price stability first; the decision settles whether a stalled labour market outweighs that.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The yearly meeting of leaders from the world's largest economies, together about 85% of global output. The rotating presidency sets the agenda, and its communiqués steer trade and debt talks without binding anyone.
g20-2026-miami.recent: The US holds the presidency after a Trump-Xi summit that produced an AI communication channel between China and the US but no breakthrough agreement, and Xi skipped the UN afterward. A US-India trade deal is not imminent, Greer says. Both are unfinished business among G20 members when the leaders meet.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets about every six weeks to set interest rates for the countries that share the euro. Its decisions reach mortgages, government borrowing costs and the euro's exchange rate.
ecb-2026-12.recent: Officials judged September's hike proportionate and said policy still does not restrict growth, with inflation at 3.8%, nearly double the target. The council meets weeks before Isabel Schnabel, its leading voice for tighter policy, leaves on 3 January, and Moulin has said France needs no help from the bank yet.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's nine-member Monetary Policy Committee, which meets eight times a year to set Bank Rate. Its vote feeds through to UK mortgage and savings rates and business loans, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-12.recent: The committee decides in a month when most Federal Reserve officials expect another rate hike by year-end and major banks are betting on a December ECB rise. The meeting settles whether the Bank of England's own borrowing costs move with them or part ways.

boj-2026-12.standing: Japan's central bank, whose policy board meets eight times a year to set the short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen, the cost of the rich world's heaviest public debt, and the yen borrowing that funds trades worldwide.
boj-2026-12.recent: Three sources say the Bank of Japan is weighing a declaration that underlying inflation has reached its 2% goal, the test it has set for further rate rises. Japanese yields jumped as a global bond sell-off deepened. What this meeting settles is whether reaching the goal changes the rate itself.

fred-us-cpi-2026-10-14.standing: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly measure of what US households pay for a fixed basket of goods and services. It is the inflation reading that Fed rate expectations, Treasury yields and Social Security adjustments move on.
fred-us-cpi-2026-10-14.recent: Federal Reserve officials are split: most expect another rate hike by year-end, yet hiring stalled at 29,000 jobs in September. This release is the price half of that argument, and it lands with crude back above $100, so it shows whether energy costs have spread into what US households pay for everything else.

fred-us-ppi-2026-10-15.standing: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly measure of the prices US producers receive for goods and services. It shows cost pressure before it reaches shop shelves, and feeds the inflation gauge the Federal Reserve targets.
fred-us-ppi-2026-10-15.recent: The Bureau of Labor Statistics reports the prices producers received last month. The release settles whether cost pressure at the factory gate and in wholesale services is building or easing before it reaches consumers.

fred-us-retail-sales-2026-10-15.standing: The Census Bureau's monthly estimate of what American shops, restaurants and online sellers took in. Consumer spending is about two-thirds of the US economy, so it moves growth forecasts, Treasury yields and the dollar.
fred-us-retail-sales-2026-10-15.recent: The Census Bureau reports its first estimate of last month's US retail sales, with revisions to the months before it. The release settles whether household spending held up or slowed, the largest single input to the quarter's growth figure.
